messages:
alex: quick async check — finished the microstride kernel patch on canary shard A. landed PR, ran a couple of smoke benches.

alex: what I did: applied stride-based attention tiling, toggled slot coalescing to 1.4x, adjusted batch-slot allocator to prefer hot slots.

alex: key numbers from local smoke (10k tokens total): p50 82ms -> 70ms, p95 210ms -> 168ms, tokens/s +11%. memory footprint ~ -6% on same model.

maria: nice! can you paste the perf command + flags you used? want to re-run on my machine.

alex: sure —
```
# run on canary A
./bench/run_infer --model redwood-v2-small \
  --seq 1024 --batch 1 --microstride 64 \
  --slot-coalesce 1.4 --alloc-policy hot-first \
  --trace perf.json
```

alex: also enabled kv-prefix caching for the run (ttl 45s) to simulate typical traffic.

tj: any regressions on long-context sampling? last time we saw p99 jump for seq>2048.

alex: good call — for seq 4096 p99 did increase ~8% (from 520ms -> 560ms). root cause looks like extra memcpy from stride alignment; I have a follow-up to pipeline the memcpy off-thread.

haley: blockers?

alex: blocker: the memcpy-offthread patch touches the allocator. need a quick design review because it can touch slot lifecycle. also want CI perf job to run the new config before we rollout.

maria: I'll take the allocator review. send the PR link and a short RFC comment.

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4482 — description at top of branch. brief note: the offthread memcpy uses an arena per worker and drains in background; falls back to sync copy when arena saturated.

perf-bot: perf summary for run 1718123456-canaryA:
- model: redwood-v2-small
- seq: 1024
- p50: 70ms (baseline 82ms)
- p95: 168ms (baseline 210ms)
- p99: 560ms (baseline 520ms)
- tokens/s: 11% up
- mem: 6% down

tj: thanks. can we add a microbenchmark with seq distribution [128,512,2048,4096] in the CI matrix? would catch the p99 trend earlier.

alex: adding that to the perf job — will push change to .github/workflows/perf.yml after allocator review.

haley: schedule: if allocator review by EOD today, canary run tomorrow morning and rollout to 10% on Tuesday?

maria: ack, I'll review by 5pm PT.

alex: cool — follow-ups: (1) allocator review (maria), (2) add seq-dist matrix to CI (alex), (3) memcpy-offthread safety tests (alex/tj). ping me if you want to pair on the race conditions. :thumbsup:

tj: I'll add a small harness for race fuzzing — should help surface the edge cases.

haley: thanks team — rolling updates please.

alex: updating the PR with microbench numbers and a short runbook for rollback.

maria: LGTM on first pass, adding small comment.

alex: thanks — I'll post a short postmortem-style note in #eng-runtime when we finish the canary run.
